attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own newsletter, in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'Will begin to unwind' is firm language, so this is a scorable conditional forecast. Reading 'the implications' as those of inherent LLM limitations, and 'the whole thing' as the AI bubble, follows from the surrounding paragraphs. The antecedent is kept, and the nearby hedged 2026 line ('will likely') is correctly left out as a deadline.

contract.note: The plain reading (a broad retreat in AI valuations, funding or investment, tied to recognition of the limitations) is fair and ordinary. Treating the claim as open-ended is right because no deadline is given. 'Fully appreciated' has no threshold, so the result depends on how that condition is interpreted.

evidence.note: A March 2026 survey shows general bubble worry among retail investors. It does not show recognition of inherent LLM limitations, and it says nothing about any unwinding.
An April 2026 institutional survey finds most investors expect real AI benefits while seeing valuations as stretched. This does not establish the condition and is not an outcome measure.
The Bank of England reports AI valuations outpacing the wider market in Q2 2026. That shows no unwinding then, but it cannot contradict an open-ended conditional forecast.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm conditional forecast with no deadline. The packet does not show the condition was met: the surveys measure bubble worry, not acceptance of inherent LLM limitations. Q2 2026 valuations were still rising, and the one October pullback report could not be read. Since the condition's status is unknown, the forecast cannot be scored, and continued growth so far does not contradict it.
